//: House numbers that get tuned (standing rule 27, AR9). Standards constants — WCAG's 4.5, 3.0, three flashes per second, the 10% luminance change, 341x256 px — are pinned in the code with the reason, not here.

derivation.//: DI3, Carbon's grammar: hover is one step (a half until 3.1.0 — Kenny found it too faint on the showcase, KT8/H1), selected one, active two. Expressed in OKLCh lightness so a step looks the same size in every theme (AR4).

perceptualDistanceFloor.//: DI4. Not a standard — WCAG has no such threshold. Below roughly 10 two colours read as the same; 12 leaves a margin.

textureOpacityCeiling.//: DI9, from THEMING.md: the register layer must be felt, not seen. Advice rather than a gate since 2026-09-09 [Kenny]: `npm run advice` measures every theme against this one number and prints what it finds. The per-theme exception list that used to sit here is gone with the gate — a theme whose approved demo measured a stronger texture (phantom 0.14, dark 0.35, blueprint 0.18 at the time this was removed) now simply reads as over the ceiling in the advice, which is what it always was.

stateVisibilityFloor.why: KT2: how far a pressed state must sit from its base colour before someone can see that they pressed it. House number on the same OKLab scale as perceptualDistanceFloor, not a standard — WCAG says nothing about state changes. Five themes reach 10.0 to 12.1 today; cyberpunk and terminal reach 2.6 to 8.4.

badgePlateFloor.why: KT2-3: how far a status badge's plate must sit from the surface under it before it stops reading as a badge. Deliberately low — the label carries the meaning (DI4), so the plate only has to read as a plate. Measured 2026-09-04: the worst plate sits 5.6 from its card (terminal, withdrawn). This is a floor against a future palette flattening a badge into its card, not a claim that 5 is comfortable.

overflow.//: TH99, AR26. The three widths the overflow and rhythm gate measures every example page at, and the floor under which two stacked blocks count as touching.
overflow.widthsWhy: 320 is the narrowest viewport WCAG SC 1.4.10 asks a page to reflow into, 768 is the tablet edge where a side column drops below, 1280 is the desktop width the rest of the browser suite already uses.
overflow.minBlockGapWhy: The fault is two blocks TOUCHING — a gap of zero, which is what the chassis kit shipped. Two pixels is the floor that catches that without turning a deliberate 4px heading margin into a violation; it is not a claim that 2px is comfortable spacing.

fontsBudgetBytes.why: AR39: the shipped faces one theme names may weigh this much together. The critic measured 9-18 kB per latin woff2 face and priced the first draft's 3 MB as slack; woodblock and lapis ship a script subset beside latin and are the themes this number is really about. An operational knob (standing rule 27), not a standard. Kenny raised it for woodblock alone on 2026-09-08 (R6-Q6): its two Japanese families need a real bold face each, measured at 2,375,188 bytes together, and a synthesised bold thickens a Japanese stroke where a real face redraws it.

perTheme.//: A theme whose families cannot fit the shared number, each with the reason and the date Kenny raised it.

stylesheets.//: The one stylesheet list every CSS gate reads [TH130]: a file and the roles it plays. authored: a human writes it and check-layers holds its colour discipline; generated: a generator writes it; bundled: dist/kp-themes.css concatenates it, in this order; classes: it declares class names (check-utilities, check-migration); motion: it may carry animations (check-motion); texture: it may declare --fx-texture (check-texture). gates.test.mjs refuses a css/ file in the manifest that has no entry here, so a new stylesheet cannot slip past a gate by being absent from its private list. Order matters for `bundled` only.
